Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "Northline Boardworks announced today that its new Tideway range of surfboards, skateboards, and snowboards will be available through participating shops beginning September 12. The range brings together three board types under one design program, but each model was developed for its own conditions and use. The company said the launch follows two years of work with riders, repair technicians, and independent retailers. Tideway boards will be offered in several sizes, with model details and regional stock information listed on Northline’s website.

The announcement covers equipment made at Northline’s workshop in Astoria, Oregon, and at two partner facilities in British Columbia and Washington. Surfboard blanks are shaped in Astoria, while skateboard decks are pressed at the Washington facility. Snowboard cores and finished boards are produced in British Columbia. Northline said that the three sites use the same inspection checklist, although the materials and manufacturing steps differ by board type. The company has not said that the range will replace any existing models; several current boards will remain in the catalog during the fall season.

Northline product director Lena Ortiz said the goal was to make the range easier to understand without treating different sports as interchangeable. “A surfboard, a skateboard, and a snowboard ask different things of the person riding them,” Ortiz said. “We wanted the shared design choices to make sense across the collection, while keeping the shape and flex appropriate to each board.” The collection uses a small set of common colors and graphic marks, but the deck shapes, surface finishes, and hardware vary by model. Riders can choose from the standard Tideway graphics or a plain finish on selected sizes.

The main equipment details are:

1. **Tideway Surf:** The surfboards use a recycled-foam core with fiberglass reinforcement and a bio-based resin. They will be sold in five lengths, from 6 feet 2 inches to 9 feet. Each board includes a removable fin system and a repair card identifying the resin and reinforcement used. Northline describes the boards as suitable for a range of everyday conditions, not as a replacement for a rider’s judgment about local surf or weather.

2. **Tideway Street:** The skateboards have seven-ply maple decks sourced from mills in the Pacific Northwest, with a medium concave shape and two deck widths. Trucks, wheels, and bearings are sold separately, so customers can select parts to suit their setup. The standard graphic is printed with water-based ink. Northline said the deck has passed its regular flex and impact checks, but it has not been rated for a particular riding style or skill level.

3. **Tideway Alpine:** The snowboards have wood cores, sintered bases, and steel edges, with four lengths for different rider preferences. The company lists a directional shape and a medium flex rating for the initial model. Bindings are not included. Northline advises customers to check binding compatibility and consult a qualified shop when selecting equipment, particularly if they are replacing parts from another setup.

4. **Care and repair:** Each board comes with a basic care sheet covering cleaning, storage, and routine inspection. Surfboard repairs should be handled with materials compatible with the board’s resin system. Skateboard and snowboard owners can bring eligible boards to participating shops for inspection; repair cost and timing will depend on the damage and the shop’s capacity. The care sheet includes contact details for Northline’s service desk.

Northline said the use of recycled foam in the surfboards is limited to the core material and does not mean that every component is recycled. The company also noted that the maple decks are made from wood, not from a composite substitute. Its materials page identifies the listed suppliers and explains which components are covered by each sourcing statement. Northline has not published a full life-cycle assessment for the range. It plans to review material availability and customer feedback after the first season before deciding whether to make changes to later production runs.

Before release, staff from the three facilities checked the boards for visible defects, dimensions, and the finish specified for each model. Northline also arranged riding sessions with a small group of local testers. Those sessions were intended to gather feedback on fit, feel, and handling; they were not presented as a controlled safety study. The company said comments from testers led to adjustments to the surfboard fin boxes and the placement of the snowboard graphics. No tester quotes or performance comparisons were included in the launch materials.

Retailers will receive a product guide with board dimensions, component notes, and care information. Northline said participating shops can request staff training on the range, with sessions offered in person or online. The company will publish a list of participating shops on September 5, one week before the scheduled availability date. Individual stores may not carry every model or size, and customers are advised to contact a shop directly to confirm stock. Online orders will be limited to destinations Northline can serve through its current shipping arrangements.

Ortiz said, “We’re glad to have the first Tideway boards ready for riders and shops to see. The details matter, especially when a collection crosses several board sports, so we’ve tried to make the specifications clear and the care information useful.” Northline said it will collect questions through its service desk and update the online product pages if customers or retailers identify information that needs clarification.
